I will keep my land in the usual Quzhou pattern: one season of winter wheat and one season of summer maize on the same field. I am 70, so I will not spread myself across many crops. I want one familiar system, simple field work, steady grain, and work that can be done with village machinery. In Quzhou, the rain is mainly in summer, so wheat still needs irrigation, while maize can lean more on rainfall. I will use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed, keep fertilizer moderate instead of chasing the very highest input level, return straw to the field, and avoid too many pesticide sprays. I will manage wheat more carefully for water, and maize more carefully for density, weeds, and late-season disease and insects. I am assuming I farm 8 mu, and I will put all 8 mu into the same wheat-maize rotation because that is the crop mix I trust most and can still manage well at my age.
